content.user_title: Refactor Go Code with Tests and Human Review
content.value_statement: Large Go refactors can break callers, hide behavior changes, and create conflicting pull requests. This skill guides tool-driven changes with targeted tests and staged human review.
actual_capabilities: Guide dependency mapping with gopls references, call hierarchy, and exported API inspection before proposing a refactoring inventory.
Select characterization tests or targeted tests based on coverage of the affected code.
Match common refactorings to gopls actions, gofmt rewrites, eg templates, gopatch, or custom analysis fixers.
Plan import-cycle fixes using consumer-side interfaces and incremental type moves using compatibility aliases.
Sequence atomic changes into separate worktrees and human-reviewed pull requests while avoiding overlapping parallel edits.
Specify build, vet, test, race detection, coverage, and benchmark checks appropriate to each change.
limitations: Requires a Go project, git, and gopls; optional workflows need additional tools and repository permissions.
Provides instructions and examples, not a bundled executable refactoring engine.
Cannot guarantee behavior preservation for reflection, struct tags, external callers, or untested paths.
Requires human approval for staged changes; companion skills cover naming conventions, target layouts, and full gopls setup.

use_cases.title: Split an Overgrown Function
use_cases.description: Assess affected code, add missing tests, and extract a focused helper without combining the change with a feature.

use_cases.title: Migrate a Shared Package
use_cases.description: Plan compatibility aliases, caller migration, dependency ordering, and staged reviews for a type moved between packages.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Multi-Step Refactor
use_cases.description: Build a change inventory, isolate worktrees, and schedule independent pull requests without parallelizing overlapping symbol edits.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Rename
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [symbol] and propose a safe rename to [new name]. Identify references, reflection risks, and verification steps. Wait for approval before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Extract a Tested Helper
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan extracting [responsibility] from [function]. Measure affected coverage, propose missing tests, and choose a gopls action. Present the plan before changing code.

prompt_templates.title: Move a Public Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan moving [type] from [old package] to [new package]. Include aliases, import-cycle checks, external caller risks, and incremental migration checkpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: preserve compatibility during a package migration

prompt_templates.title: Stage a Repository Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an inventory for [refactoring goal]. Classify risk and structural versus behavioral changes. Order dependencies, identify parallel work, and define tests and approval gates.

output_examples.input: Plan extracting validation from a long order-processing function with limited tests.
output: Assessment: affected validation paths need characterization tests before extraction.
Plan: capture current success and failure results, then extract only the validation responsibility.
Verification: review the extraction diff and run build, vet, and targeted tests.
Checkpoint: obtain approval before editing; keep behavior changes outside this refactor.

output_examples.input: Plan moving a public invoice type into a billing package without breaking callers.
output: Assessment: inspect callers, package dependencies, exported methods, and reflection-sensitive uses.
Stage one: introduce the type in the destination and preserve the old name through a compatibility alias.
Stage two: migrate callers incrementally in reviewed pull requests.
Stage three: remove the deprecated alias only after reference checks and the required compatibility review.

best_practices: Approve a refactoring inventory before editing and request new approval when the scope or risk changes.
Measure coverage on affected paths and add characterization tests before restructuring poorly tested code.
Keep each change atomic, inspect tool-generated diffs, and verify build, tests, reflection-sensitive references, and relevant benchmarks.
anti_patterns: Mixing a rename or package move with a bug fix or feature in the same pull request.
Running a workspace-wide rename concurrently with other changes that could touch the same symbols.
Treating passing tests or a mechanical rewrite as proof that reflection, external consumers, and security behavior remain unchanged.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares compatibility with Codex and Claude Code for Go projects.

faq.question: What dependencies are required?
faq.answer: Go, git, and gopls are required. Optional tools include benchstat, golangci-lint, deadcode, eg, and gopatch.

faq.question: Can it refactor code without tests?
faq.answer: It recommends characterization tests first and requires human approval before refactoring untested code.

faq.question: Does gopls guarantee every change is safe?
faq.answer: No. Extraction needs careful verification, and reflection, tags, templates, and external callers can escape static checks.

faq.question: How does it handle public type moves?
faq.answer: It recommends compatibility aliases, incremental caller migration, deprecation, and approval before removing old names.

faq.question: Does the workflow merge changes automatically?
faq.answer: The staged workflow requires humans to review and merge each intermediate pull request. The final integration pull request starts as a draft.
